note_tweet.text:
Watch BotPsy in action with this capability demo:

BotPsy, our latest 0.8B tool-calling model, was given six travel tools and four requests about a trip to Rome.

It runs on an old M1 MacBook Air with no cloud calls, and the model file is 812 MB.

Asked for the cheapest flight from Paris to Rome on 14 December, BotPsy passed over a €49 flight on the 13th and picked the €71 one on the 14th. Over the next three requests it reported rain on the 15th and 16th, found the cheapest hotel rated 8 or more and booked it for 3 nights.

All six tools return mock data, and the booking charges nothing. The video is sped up and shows each reply's real response time.

https://t.co/paHz2R5UoA

The app runs the call, sends back the result, and BotPsy keeps going until the task is done.

note_tweet.text:
VoxDance Lab has released VoxMel, a speech-synthesis model designed to generate voices it was not specifically trained to copy.

The technical approach targets the hardest part of voice generation: producing natural-sounding speech from limited information about a speaker. If the model performs as described, it could make voice cloning more flexible—but also raises the usual consent and impersonation risks because zero-shot systems reduce the data needed to reproduce a voice.

https://t.co/ILD1vvdBhU

On ERNIE 5.5 Flash, ERNIE Evolve tackled three inference optimization challenges:
• Low-latency inference: Streamlined execution and communication paths on Kunlunxin P800, reaching 623.6% of baseline generation speed.
• Deterministic inference: Optimized sampling and attention, reaching 133.7% of baseline throughput while preserving bitwise determinism.
• GPU decoding: Improved MoE scheduling and kernel execution, reaching 114.9% of baseline decoding speed with no accuracy loss.
All three optimizations underwent rigorous load testing and correctness validation.

note_tweet.text:
Introducing ERNIE Evolve, our automated research system for improving AI training and inference. ⚙️

Given a clear research goal, it selects research directions, modifies code and runs experiments. Only improvements that pass independent evaluation and review are kept, and each round’s findings guide the next.

From public benchmarks to ERNIE 5.5 Flash inference tests, here’s what it achieved:
- SOTA on NanoChat AutoResearch and NanoGPT Speedrun
- 33.7% higher deterministic GPU inference throughput
- 14.9% faster single-request decoding on GPUs

This is a practical step toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Next, we plan to extend this approach to training systems, model capabilities and evaluation.
